purpose: Teach: 女児/インサイダー/安保理/郵政省/運輸省/建設省/日本共産党/中共

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、女児虐待防止策の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you wrote your paper on preventing child abuse against girls, didn't you?
lines.style: Steady, observant, gentle confirmation. Leaning in slightly with genuine interest. Warm eye contact. The tone of someone who has read the work and noticed something in it.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、企業のインサイダー取引研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I wrote my paper on insider trading at corporations.
lines.style: Clear and direct, no defensiveness. Slight pause before answering, as if collecting the right framing. Earnest but not apologetic. A quiet correction stated plainly.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、国連安保理の歴史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper covered the history of the UN Security Council, didn't it?
lines.style: Gentle, thoughtful pause before the question. Testing whether he'll correct her again. Reflective tone — almost musing. Still warm, not accusatory.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、旧郵政省の民営化研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I wrote my paper on the privatization of the old Postal Ministry.
lines.style: Same clarity as before. Direct. A pattern emerging in his corrections. No frustration, just factual. Settling into the rhythm of being listened to.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 旧運輸省の組織改編史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: You covered the organizational restructuring of the old Ministry of Transport, didn't you?
lines.style: Engaged now, leaning in with genuine understanding. A shift in her tone — no longer testing, but acknowledging the thread. Warm curiosity, not confusion.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、旧建設省の公共事業史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — my paper was on the public works history of the old Ministry of Construction.
lines.style: Steady, almost relieved. He's being heard. The corrections feel less like corrections now and more like precision. Slight ease in his delivery.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、日本共産党の戦後史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper was on the postwar history of the Japanese Communist Party, right?
lines.style: Reflective, thoughtful. A deeper question now — she's testing her own understanding. Gentle, not accusatory. The tone of someone who wants to get it right.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、中共政府と日本外交の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I wrote on China's diplomatic relations with Japan and the government's role.
lines.style: Final correction, delivered with the same quiet precision. A closing statement. Calm, clear, ready to move forward. The smallest note of finality.
